# Hash-pinned install set for the OTLP extra baked into the root Dockerfile.
#
# Direct requirements: opentelemetry-proto>=1.20.0 protobuf>=4.21.0
#
# That range install is what this file replaces. `docker build -t clawmetry .`
# is a documented way to run this project (README, CLAUDE.md "Deploy"), and
# until now the image resolved these two names live at build time against a
# floor of `protobuf>=4.21.0` -- a range that has spanned four major versions.
# Two identical `docker build` invocations a week apart could bake different
# bytes into the receiver that an org then points OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
# at. The base image is already pinned by digest for exactly this reason (see
# the FROM line's comment); this is the same argument applied to the layer
# directly above it, which was the last unpinned resolve left in the file that
# is not the code under test.
#
# Deliberately a SECOND file rather than reusing ci-otel-extra.txt, which
# pins the same two names at the same versions. That file describes ci.yml's
# otlp-receiver JOB, and the two move for different reasons: a CI-motivated
# edit there must not silently change what ships in the image. Same names
# today, separate reasons to change, so separate files.
#
# Not folded into requirements.txt either. These are the optional `otel`
# extra (setup.py), baked in on purpose because a receiver that answers 501
# to http/protobuf until someone runs `pip install clawmetry[otel]` is not a
# receiver. Adding them to requirements.txt would install them for every pip
# user as well, which is the opposite of what the extra is for.
#
# Installed with `pip install --require-hashes`, which refuses to install
# anything not listed here with a matching hash -- so the image gets the exact
# artifacts this file names, or the build fails. Every transitive dependency
# is present because --require-hashes demands the whole closure; here the
# closure is just these two names (opentelemetry-proto requires protobuf,
# protobuf requires nothing), which is why the file is this short.
#
# Each version lists the sha256 of EVERY distribution PyPI publishes for it
# (wheels for each platform, plus the sdist). pip accepts a download that
# matches any one of them, so the pin does not quietly depend on the builder
# resolving to the same wheel this file was generated against -- an arm64
# laptop and an amd64 runner both build from this file.
#
# On the interpreter: the base image is python:3.14-slim. protobuf 7.36.1
# ships a cp310-abi3 manylinux wheel, which is ABI-compatible with 3.14, and
# opentelemetry-proto 1.44.0 is a pure-python py3-none-any wheel. Both
# declare requires_python >=3.10. A protobuf release that drops the abi3
# wheel would need this checked again before the bump lands.
#
# Updating: the `/.github/requirements` pip entry in .github/dependabot.yml
# advances this file and rewrites the --hash lines along with the version, so
# a bump arrives already verifiable. Without that entry the pin would simply
# freeze the image at today's CVEs, which is the other end of the same
# problem the unpinned range was at.

opentelemetry-proto==1.45.0 \
    --hash=sha256:96ee414f24bc3f61ea8e17dc56b4348d4049d73db3eb17c6b3edf75b5b403300 \
    --hash=sha256:9731566359d7b8e1ee1e149d8e4ad6865bab965e657ad3387ec2784d16927666
protobuf==7.36.2 \
    --hash=sha256:497d0463ff3316681da6c0b9e8d06cb465d61abce00b613ab42226175644d1bb \
    --hash=sha256:89f23aa53c24553a2416fd4fd1ec06f74fa42b14b546d8883128813f775bbfd2 \
    --hash=sha256:912c1221170e16c08d1f086762f563dd61ff83c18b5fa6652952dfaded66f728 \
    --hash=sha256:a300819d441e078a5608c0d3c709796bb548136058fda017ae51d425b44fd353 \
    --hash=sha256:bdb3a345d48db958e6ce1f18e508beb0cc981d64f24088427549c866cd039f1e \
    --hash=sha256:cbc70b17ee27e28894c7fee8bb04be1abead49e936bc70eb60052531eee2079e \
    --hash=sha256:e11e1f0180583a2af89db6a2ecd9e8dc40aa6d2988ca175bfd0e6d12ea72d74e \
    --hash=sha256:f4fee11ec330d238b34a05c9b675f693c20415d1c5bd7d5320cc2f8a798eb9cf
